text:
Arjun: Heads-up: spotted an inconsistent exception from the Python SDK async client — when a request times out we get asyncio.CancelledError with no HTTP context or request_id. Makes retries/telemetry hard.

Sara: Can you paste a minimal repro + traceback?

Arjun: Sure, pasted below. This is from an internal test hitting our hosted API with a short timeout:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/app/test_async.py", line 42, in test_timeout
    await client.responses.create(prompt="hi", max_tokens=1)
asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError
```
No wrapping exception, no .status_code, nothing. The request_id header from the server shows up in logs but never surfaces to the caller.

Morgan: I think this happens when the aiohttp layer cancels before we process response bytes. Our current code only constructs HTTPError in the JSON decoding path (i.e. after response body read). If timeout/cancel happens earlier we bubble raw CancelledError.

Jamal: Agreed — we should have a single canonical exception type for HTTP failures (ClientHTTPError) for both sync/async flows. It should carry: `status_code` (int|None), `request_id` (str|None), `raw_body` (bytes|None), and preserve the original exception as `__cause__`. Also update typings so callers can `except ClientHTTPError as e:` and access those attrs.

Arjun: Proposed quick fix: catch `asyncio.CancelledError` and `asyncio.TimeoutError` in the client request path, and re-raise `AsyncHTTPTimeout(ClientHTTPError)` with any headers/body we have access to. Important: don't attempt to `json.loads` if body is bytes; preserve raw bytes on the exception so integrators can decide.

Morgan: I'll open a PR. Plan:
- unify exception hierarchy (BaseClientError -> ClientHTTPError -> AsyncHTTPTimeout)
- ensure `ClientHTTPError.raw_body` is `bytes|None` and included in str(e) summary (truncated)
- surface `request_id` from `X-Request-Id` or `request-id` headers
- add type stubs so raises are part of the client method signatures
- tests for: timeout path, non-json body, header propagation

Sara: Small DX ask: can we also add an `async with Client.timeout(seconds)` convenience to set per-call timeouts instead of passing `timeout=` everywhere? Would reduce user mistake surface area.

Jamal: One caution: we must not swallow cancellation semantics for callers that expect task cancellation to propagate. Wrapping CancelledError into a different subclass might be surprising. Better to wrap but set `__cause__` and keep original CancelledError type reachable (e.g., AsyncHTTPTimeout.__cause__ = CancelledError). Document behavior clearly.

devx-bot: Linked issue DEVEX-412 and added label `sdk:errors`. CI will run on PR.

Arjun: Thanks — assigning to @Morgan. I'll drop a small repro gist in the PR and include the server-side sample that sets `X-Request-Id` so we can assert propagation.

Morgan: On it. Expect PR by EOD, will ping here with the diff + unit tests. :thumbsup:
